text: In Chennai, homes, hospitals and emergency
services depend on connected networks.
ORCA explores how an emulated satellite
backed network can protect these everyday
services.
An attacker uses stolen credentials to
reach the satellite operator’s ground
management network.
Terminals are disrupted.
A backup path may also be
unsafe, and service providers need to
be told.
ORCA collects telemetry and prepares features.
Model one detects anomalies.
Model two forecasts failure in minutes.
Model three distinguishes faults from attacks,
or abstains.
Model four allocates limited capacity.
Role agents coordinate around the evidence.
Retrieval searches the knowledge base for
relevant sources.
A deterministic rule engine applies verified
records and returns cited verdicts.
The agents explain; the human remains
accountable.
Before a fix, ORCA checks the
backup path and tests the plan
in a clone.
In assisted mode, a human approves
the exact plan.
The change rolls out in stages:
five, twenty five, then one hundred
percent.
Re-attack checks and rollback guard the
result.
Services can recover while a hash
chained audit preserves the evidence.
The gap analyst records potential policy
gaps for human review.
Models detect, agents coordinate, code
decides, and humans approve.
